title: Introduce atomic CI lifecycle and dependency concierge
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: Introduces an atomic CI lifecycle orchestrator, consolidates premerge steps into stage-aware lifecycles, and adds a lightweight 'dependency concierge' that annotates and stages dependency bumps to reduce presubmit churn.
description:
Context and motivation: Our presubmit and release pipelines have accumulated multiple ad-hoc stages (lint, unit, integration, smoke, release-smoke) with duplicated bootstrap logic. This causes frequent CI flakiness, long feedback loops for dependency upgrades, and high cognitive overhead when adding new stages. ENG-2419 asked for clearer lifecycle boundaries and ENG-2460 requested less disruptive dep bumps. This PR delivers two complementary pieces: (1) an 'atomic CI lifecycle' abstraction that models presubmit/release pipelines as discrete, idempotent stages with explicit transitions and health probes, and (2) a 'dependency concierge' helper that annotates dependency upgrade PRs with recommended presubmit lanes, a lightweight staging window, and optional auto-quarantine for risky transitive changes.

What changed (high level): - Introduced ci/lifecycle package that provides lifecycle manifests, stage adapters, and a small state machine used by our composite actions. - Consolidated bootstrap scripts into a single hermetic Go entrypoint used by all lint/test actions. - Added a dependency-concierge service (serverless) that runs during PR creation to evaluate dependency graphs and annotate PRs with suggested presubmit lanes and a compatibility score. - Updated GitHub Action workflows to use stage-aware dispatch events and to skip unnecessary heavy lanes for low-risk changes. - Added telemetry hooks so stages emit a short 'stage-latency' and 'stage-success' metric for Console dashboards.

Checklist: - [x] ci/lifecycle implementation with unit tests - [x] Go hermetic entrypoint + small shim for composite actions - [x] dependency concierge prototype + integration test - [x] workflow updates across .github/workflows/* - [x] docs: doc/ci/lifecycles.md and PR template updates - [x] e2e smoke on staging CI and canary rollout to main CI

How to exercise locally: 1) make sure Golang >=1.21 is active, run `go test ./ci/lifecycle -v` 2) run `make ci-bootstrap` to build `bin/ci-bootstrap` then `./bin/ci-bootstrap --stage=lint --repo=redwood` to emulate a stage run 3) dependency concierge can be invoked locally with `go run ./tools/depconcierge --pr=12345 --repo=redwood`

Backwards compatibility / risk: The lifecycle abstraction is additive; existing composite actions are migrated gradually. Workflows default to an adapter that preserves old semantics unless a lifecycle manifest is referenced. The dependency concierge only annotates PRs and never merges; auto-quarantine is opt-in per repository.

Commits summary: ["feat(ci): add lifecycle state machine and manifests", "refactor(ci): converge bootstrap into hermetic go entrypoint", "feat(dep): add dependency-concierge annotator and scoring", "ci(workflows): migrate release and presubmit workflows to stage-aware dispatch", "docs: add lifecycle docs and update PR template", "test: add unit/integration tests for lifecycle and concierge"]

Changed files (high level): ["ci/lifecycle/state_machine.go", "ci/lifecycle/manifest.go", "cmd/ci-bootstrap/main.go", "tools/depconcierge/main.go", ".github/workflows/presubmit.yml", ".github/workflows/release.yml", "docs/ci/lifecycles.md", "internal/telemetry/stage_metrics.go", "Makefile", "go.mod", "go.sum", "scripts/action-shims/adapter.sh", "templates/pr_template.md", "tests/integration/depconcierge_test.go", "tests/unit/lifecycle_test.go"]

Representative diffs/snippets: ["ci/lifecycle/state_machine.go: added Transition() and Probe() with conservative retry policy (3 attempts, exponential backoff)", "cmd/ci-bootstrap/main.go: replaced multiple shell bootstraps with single Go binary that initializes toolchain and validates env vars", ".github/workflows/presubmit.yml: switched from matrix all -> stage-aware dispatch; added 'fast-lint' lane for docs-only changes"]

Review conversation (summary): "Jacob Lee: suggested tightening the retry policy and adding a metric for 'quarantine_count' to watch dep quarantines; asked for an explicit flag to opt-out per-repo. Response (Aisha): tightened retry policy to 3 attempts and added opt-out flag 'CI_LIFECYCLE_DISABLED' and 'dep-concierge.disabled' repo annotation. Sofia Martinez: flagged potential surge cost if dependency concierge runs full graph evaluation on large monorepos; asked for sampling and budget caps. Response: added a conservative sampling mode and a per-repo budget cap in the concierge config; integration test added. Liam O'Connor: requested to keep old bootstrap for one release window in case of regressions. Response: kept legacy adapter which delegates to the new binary unless env var 'CI_BOOTSTRAP_LEGACY' is set to 'false'. QA: QA ran presubmit smoke and staging canary (10% of runs) for 72 hours with no regressions observed. CI status: initial pipeline hit flaky integration tests, addressed by increasing test shard timeout and rerunning; final run green. Approvals: Jacob Lee approved (2026-03-03), Sofia Martinez approved (2026-03-04), Liam O'Connor approved (2026-03-04). Merge decision: squash-and-merge after green CI and two approvals. Merge method: squash/merge. Post-merge tasks: - Monitor stage_latency and quarantine_count in Console for two weeks - Ramp concierge scoring threshold from conservative -> default over 1 week - Announce change in #infra and update developer onboarding docs"

Where this differs from previous work: unlike previous monolithic presubmit refactors, this PR intentionally models stages as first-class atomic units with health probes and backward-compatible adapters. The dependency concierge is designed to reduce human noise by giving presubmit recommendations rather than auto-routing or automatic merges.

Notes and rationale: - Primary goal: shorten feedback loops for low-risk changes by avoiding heavy lanes and reduce presubmit churn for dependency bumps. - Secondary goal: create a small, testable runtime for lifecycle orchestration that can be reused for Dedicated and Private installer release flows.

Known follow-ups (tracking): - ENG-2501: add staged canary promotion for release workflows - ENG-2502: expand dep-concierge to surface vulnerable transitive deps and suggested mitigation - ENG-2503: expose lifecycle traces in tracing UI for faster debugging

notes: This PR is intentionally staged: workflows reference lifecycle manifests by name so we can migrate repos one-by-one. See docs/ci/lifecycles.md for migration steps. The concierge uses limited CPU per-run and caches evaluation results in a short TTL to avoid repeated heavy evaluations.
